newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: At least 75 Colombian rebels lay down arms.
newsitem.headline: At least 75 Colombian rebels lay down arms.

text.p: At least 75 leftist guerrillas, including a rebel chieftain linked to a peasant massacre, laid down their arms on Monday and surrendered to the authorities, officials said.
Guerrilla leader David Mesa Pena demobilized with 50 of his comrades from the Maoist People's Liberation Army (EPL), the country's third guerrilla force in northwestern Antioquia province.

Another 24 rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), Colombia's oldest and largest rebel group, handed themselves over in the troubled banana-growing region of Uraba, also in Antioquia.
There was confusion over the number of rebels who turned themselves in, with reporters at the scene initially referring to the handover of more than 100 guerrilla fighters.

Authorities confirmed a total of 75, however. Antioquia Gov. Alvaro Uribe hailed the handovers and said more were expected to occur later in the week. "This should serve as an example to other rebels to take advantage of the government's reintegration policy," he said.
The province has been the scene of some of the most violent clashes and heaviest guerrilla losses since the rebels unleashed their bloodiest offensive in decades one month ago.

In fighting 10 days ago, Uribe said at least 60 guerrillas had been killed. Two days earlier, the military said it had killed 25 FARC rebels after ordering air strikes on a highway they had been blocking for a week.
A defence attache at one embassy said a series of factors probably prompted the surrender but doubted it was a sign of widespread demoralisation following recent heavy casualties.

Political analysts have highlighted internal divisions in the EPL, thought to number about 1,000 fighters, since the mainstream laid down arms in 1990. Monday's surrender is the second major blow to the EPL ranks since 50 other rebels laid down their weapons in July.

Mesa Pena, alias Gonzalo, has been linked in military intelligence reports to scores of killings, including the massacre of 16 peasants in Uraba in May. He is also said to have headed a campaign to kill former EPL members who demobilized in 1990.

Military sources say he had serious disagreements with other EPL commanders and, after a brief period of joint actions with the FARC, launched a battle for supremacy against it in an eastern corner of Antioquia.

Both the FARC and EPL contingents surrendered to a right-wing paramilitary group, which has long been involved in a bitter conflict with the insurgents particularly for control of lucrative contraband routes in Uraba.
